findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the Observation: `rebar audit serve` does not pass an explicit `repo_root` (`_audit_commands.py:107` calls `server.serve(host=host, port=port)`). Either cover the audit-serve read path in the spawn-count AC, or make the CLI pass the resolved root.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_audit_commands.py:107: `server.serve(host=host, port=port)`, with no `repo_root` argument

src/rebar/audit/server.py:167: `def serve(*, host: str = "127.0.0.1", port: int = 8765, repo_root: str | None = None)`; line 172 `create_app(repo_root)`; lines 105/119 pass `repo_root` (None) to `list_tickets` and `audit_trail`

Prerequisite ticket 40c3-d22a-3872-4c8c measured audit `GET /` at 10 `ensure_fresh` spawns with `REBAR_ROOT` unset, against 5 with it set. That only happens if audit serve does NOT pass an explicit root.
findings.finding: The plan says `rebar audit serve` passes an explicit `repo_root` and so already spawns 0 git processes. The code shows it passes none: the CLI calls `server.serve(host=host, port=port)` without `repo_root`, and `serve`/`create_app`/`_audited_tickets` default it to None. Every audited read therefore takes the git `rev-parse --show-toplevel` path when `REBAR_ROOT` is unset.
findings.location: Observation — "With `REBAR_ROOT` set, or an explicit `repo_root` (as `rebar audit serve` passes), the same reads spawn 0."
scenarios: `rebar audit serve` started without `REBAR_ROOT`: each index request does `list_tickets` plus 4 reads per audited ticket, and each re-runs `repo_root` discovery. This is the workload with the most spawns, and the plan implies it is already unaffected.
An implementer trusts the premise, never checks the audit path, and adds no audit-serve spawn test.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace "or an explicit `repo_root` (as `rebar audit serve` passes)" with "or an explicit `repo_root` argument". Then add an AC: a throttled `rebar audit serve` `GET /` with `REBAR_ROOT` unset starts at most 1 `rev-parse --show-toplevel`, shown by a spawn-count test.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the intended cache scope (per-process, keyed by cwd) and add an AC that a second show_ticket/list_tickets from the same cwd starts 0 `rev-parse --show-toplevel`.
evidence: Observation: "The root of a process's cwd does not change between reads in one process, so these are repeated lookups of the same answer."
AC1: "A library `show_ticket` ... starts at most 1 `rev-parse --show-toplevel`" (per call, not per process)
findings.finding: The Observation frames the defect as repeated lookups across reads within one process, but AC1 only bounds spawns within a single show_ticket call. A per-call dedup satisfies the AC while every subsequent read still re-spawns git.
scenarios: A long-lived library consumer calls show_ticket 100 times from the same cwd: a per-call fix still spawns 100 gits, a process-cache fix spawns 1. Both pass AC1 as written.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC: 'Two consecutive library reads from the same cwd with REBAR_ROOT unset start at most 1 `rev-parse --show-toplevel` in total, shown by the spawn-count test.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend AC1 so the spawn-count test makes two or more consecutive library reads from the same cwd and asserts at most 1 `rev-parse --show-toplevel` across all of them, not just within one show_ticket.
evidence: Title: 'Library reads rediscover the repo root with git on every call when REBAR_ROOT is unset'
Observation: 'The root of a process's cwd does not change between reads in one process, so these are repeated lookups of the same answer.'
AC1 measures one show_ticket only; it says nothing about a second read in the same process from the same cwd.
findings.finding: The spawn-count AC bounds rev-parse to at most 1 per single show_ticket call, but the headline problem is rediscovery 'on every call'. A per-call memo, rather than a process-wide one, would satisfy the AC while still spawning git on every read, which is the behavior the title says is wrong.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, AC1 ('A library show_ticket ... starts at most 1 rev-parse --show-toplevel')
scenarios: An implementation threads the root through one show_ticket call. Each call does 1 spawn, so AC1 passes, but N reads in a long-lived library or CLI-batch process still cost N spawns.
findings.suggested_fix: Change AC1 to: 'With REBAR_ROOT unset, inside a git work tree, two consecutive library reads (show_ticket then show_ticket or list_tickets) from the same cwd start at most 1 `rev-parse --show-toplevel` in total, shown by a git-spawn-count test.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either route `repo_root_or_none` (`_config_resolvers.py:225`) through the same per-cwd cache as `repo_root` and add its read-path callers (`_engine_support/reads.py:233,346`, `_store/freshness.py:67,194`) to scope, or limit AC1 to a fresh freshness marker and say why the stale-marker path is excluded.
evidence: Plan: 'every library read rediscovers the code repo root with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, through `repo_root` (`src/rebar/_config_sources.py:53`)'
Plan: 'Measured on a throwaway two-repo store with the freshness marker fresh'. The AC drops this condition.
src/rebar/_config_resolvers.py:236-243: `repo_root_or_none` runs `subprocess.run(["git", "-C", ".", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"], ...)` with no `_TOPLEVEL_BY_CWD` lookup
src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:224-233: `if marker_age < 60 and not force: return` ... `cfg_root = repo_root_or_none()`
src/rebar/_reads.py:115-116: `tracker = _tracker(repo_root)` then `_fresh(tracker)` → `ticket_reads.ensure_fresh(tracker)`
findings.finding: The plan blames only `repo_root` (`_config_sources.py:53`) for the git spawns. But `repo_root_or_none` (`src/rebar/_config_resolvers.py:225`) is a second, uncached resolver that also runs `git -C . rev-parse --show-toplevel`, and library `show_ticket` reaches it through `_fresh` → `ensure_fresh` → `repo_root_or_none()` (`_engine_support/reads.py:233`) whenever the freshness marker is 60 seconds old or more. AC1 says 'at most 1 `rev-parse --show-toplevel`' with no condition on the marker, so a stale-marker `show_ticket` starts at least 2 (one from `repo_root` on a cache miss, one from `repo_root_or_none`). The fix as scoped cannot meet AC1 in that case. Other read-path callers of the same uncached resolver are also unlisted: `_store/freshness.py:67` and `:194`, and `_load_scratch` at `_engine_support/reads.py:346`.
scenarios: An agent process calls `rebar.show_ticket` more than a minute after the last sync: `repo_root` spawns once on the cache miss and `ensure_fresh` → `repo_root_or_none` spawns again, so there are 2 toplevel lookups and AC1 is broken.
The git-spawn-count test passes only because its fixture keeps the marker fresh, so the stale-marker path stays untested and still slow.
findings.suggested_fix: Make `repo_root_or_none` use the `_TOPLEVEL_BY_CWD` cache and `_toplevel_still_valid` check, returning `None` when the cache misses and git fails. Extend the git-spawn-count test with a stale-marker case (marker age 60 seconds or more, sync enabled) that asserts at most 1 `--show-toplevel` spawn across `repo_root` and `repo_root_or_none`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the ACs so the root cache is keyed on GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE as well as cwd, and is re-checked against the filesystem (cached root still has `.git`, no nearer `.git` has appeared between cwd and root), with a test for each case.
evidence: AC2 tests only 'A cwd change between reads'.
src/rebar/_config_sources.py:58-61: 'a silently-wrong repo root is worse than a loud failure.'

The implementation keys on `(cwd, GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE)` and re-checks each hit with `_toplevel_still_valid` (lines 73-75, 101-118). The plan specifies none of this, so a cwd-only implementation would be equally compliant.
findings.finding: The only invalidation AC covers a cwd change. Git's answer for a fixed cwd also depends on the GIT_DIR and GIT_WORK_TREE environment variables and on the filesystem: the cached repo can be deleted or moved, or a nested repo can be `git init`-ed between the cwd and the cached root. A cache keyed on cwd alone passes both ACs but returns a wrong root in these cases. The code docstring at `_config_sources.py:58-61` treats a silently wrong root as worse than a loud failure, yet the plan does not require these cases to be handled.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, AC2 ('A cwd change between reads still resolves the new cwd's repo root')
scenarios: A test or tool sets GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE mid-process with an unchanged cwd. A cwd-keyed cache returns the old toplevel.

A test fixture runs `git init` in a subdirectory of an already-cached repo and reads from there. A cwd-keyed cache on the parent's entry, or a stale entry for that cwd, returns the outer repo, so the tracker and config resolve against the wrong store.
The cached repo directory is removed or moved. The cache keeps returning a path that no longer exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Add ACs: (a) changing GIT_DIR or GIT_WORK_TREE between reads with the same cwd resolves the new root; (b) `git init` in a subdirectory of a cached root, followed by a read from that subdirectory, resolves the nested repo; (c) if the cached root's `.git` is removed, the next read re-runs discovery instead of returning the stale path.

It does not say what the cache is keyed on (os.getcwd() raw or resolved through symlinks), how it is retired or invalidated beyond a cwd change, or whether it is safe under concurrent threads.
scenarios: A test suite or tool runs `git init` or removes .git in the same cwd mid-process, and a cached root (or cached absence) goes stale.
Two threads read concurrently, both miss, and both spawn git (a benign but unstated check-then-act race).

findings.finding: Behavior outside a git work tree is unspecified. AC1 is scoped to 'run from inside a git work tree', but nothing says whether a failed `rev-parse` (no repo) is cached or retried on each read, or whether the existing error and fallback behavior is preserved.
findings.location: AC1 ('run from inside a git work tree')
scenarios: A process starts outside a repo, the first read fails and the failure is cached, then the process chdirs into a repo and the cached negative result could persist if the key is mishandled.
Conversely, if failures are not cached, the not-a-repo path keeps spawning git on every read, which is fine but should be stated.
findings.suggested_fix: State the default: 'Only successful rev-parse results are cached; a failure is not cached and surfaces exactly as today.' Add a test that chdirs from a non-repo dir into a repo between reads and resolves the repo root.

evidence: The Observation contrasts REBAR_ROOT set vs unset, but no AC asserts that REBAR_ROOT and an explicit repo_root still take precedence once a cache entry exists.

findings.finding: The plan replaces per-read discovery with a reused answer but never states its correctness contract beyond 'cwd change → re-resolve'. It does not say what the reuse is keyed on, or whether a failed lookup is reused (outside a work tree, rev-parse fails). It also does not say that an explicit repo_root or REBAR_ROOT, set after a cached git lookup, still takes precedence. In-process callers that depend on fresh discovery, such as tests that create repos in tmp dirs and chdir between cases, are not acknowledged.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, AC2 ('A cwd change between reads still resolves the new cwd's repo root')
scenarios: A read from a non-repo cwd fails discovery, a failure that is reused for that cwd. `git init` then runs in that same cwd within the same process, and later reads still report no repo.
A test monkeypatches REBAR_ROOT after an earlier read in the same process has cached a git-discovered root, and the cached root wins over the env var.
The test suite reuses one tmp cwd path across cases with different repo layouts, and a process-wide answer leaks between tests.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Narrow the 'root does not change' premise to name the real invalidators (git env vars `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`, a repo created, moved or deleted under the cached path). Add ACs/tests showing a cached root is not reused when the git env vars change or a nested repo appears for the same cwd.
evidence: Plan: "The root of a process's cwd does not change between reads in one process, so these are repeated lookups of the same answer."
src/rebar/_config_sources.py:73: the cache key is `(cwd, os.environ.get("GIT_DIR"), os.environ.get("GIT_WORK_TREE"))`. The env vars change the answer for the same cwd.

src/rebar/_config_sources.py:101-118 `_toplevel_still_valid`: on each hit it re-checks that the root still has a `.git` and that no directory between root and cwd has gained one ('a repo created later'). This shows the root for a fixed cwd can change.
Plan ACs: only a cwd change is required and tested. Changes to the git env vars, nested-repo creation, and repo deletion/move are not covered.
findings.finding: The justification says "The root of a process's cwd does not change between reads in one process". That is not true in general. For the same cwd, `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` gives a different answer if `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` change, if a nested repository is created below the cached root, or if the cached repo is moved or deleted. The ACs check only that a cwd change is picked up, so a cache keyed on cwd alone would pass every AC and still return a stale root.
findings.location: Observation — final paragraph; Acceptance Criteria AC2 ("A cwd change between reads still resolves the new cwd's repo root")
scenarios: A test or long-lived process runs `git init` in a subdirectory of the cached root and then reads from there: a cwd-only cache returns the outer repo's tracker.
`GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` is set or changed in-process (e.g. by hooks or test fixtures) between reads in the same cwd.
The cached root is deleted or moved while the process keeps running (daemon threads, the reconciler).
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the sentence as: "For a fixed cwd, `GIT_DIR` and `GIT_WORK_TREE`, the toplevel answer only changes if a repository is created, moved or deleted under it, which a stat check can detect." Add ACs: (a) changing `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` between reads resolves afresh; (b) a nested `git init` below the cached root, then a read from inside it, resolves the nested root; (c) deleting the cached root's `.git` makes the lookup fall through instead of returning the stale root.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the chosen mechanism (e.g. a process-local `repo_root` cache keyed on the git-discovery inputs) and one or two sentences on why it fits better than resolving the root once per library entry point.
evidence: The plan has only 'Observation' and 'Acceptance Criteria' sections; neither names a mechanism.
'With REBAR_ROOT set, or an explicit repo_root (as rebar audit serve passes), the same reads spawn 0' shows a known zero-spawn path, but the plan never says whether to reuse it or cache instead.
src/rebar/_config_sources.py:53 `repo_root` is called from about 100 sites in src/rebar, so a cache at that layer changes behavior for all of them.
findings.finding: The plan never states which fix it is choosing or why it fits. It describes the symptom and lists ACs, but does not say whether to memoize `repo_root` in-process, resolve the root once per library entry point and pass it down as an explicit `repo_root` (the zero-spawn path the Observation itself cites for `rebar audit serve`), or something else. With no positive rationale, the trade-off between these designs is left implicit. A process-wide cache touches every `config.repo_root()` caller (dozens across the reconciler, llm, and _commands modules) and carries a staleness risk. Passing the root down per call has no staleness risk but a wider signature footprint.
findings.location: Plan body: Observation / Acceptance Criteria (no approach section)
scenarios: One implementer adds a cache inside `repo_root` and changes behavior for every caller, including long-lived reconciler or daemon threads. Another threads an explicit root through `_reads`, which fixes only show_ticket/list_tickets. Both satisfy the ACs.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an 'Approach' line: cache the result of `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` inside `_config_sources.repo_root`, keyed on the inputs git uses for discovery. This is the one choke point every read path already goes through, so it removes the repeat spawns for all callers without changing any signature.
